principle: Missing data stays missing; estimates are labeled.

changelog.title: Prospect confidence re-baseline
changelog.detail: Corrected how thin minor-league samples are discounted, reversing an unintended broad re-score while retaining protection against abrupt transition cliffs. Ranking changes on this date reflect the re-baseline, not new player performance.

changelog.title: Plate-discipline layer
changelog.detail: Added measured Swing%, Whiff%, and SwStr%, with estimated zone metrics labeled separately.

changelog.title: Methodology honesty polish
changelog.detail: Added the live forward-gate disclosure, including when the ValuCast projection is losing.

changelog.title: Ahead-of-the-Curve scorecard v2
changelog.detail: Pre-registered controlled, exit-accounted targets before scoring public divergence calls.

changelog.title: Saves and holds split
changelog.detail: Separated saves and holds targets before combining them for SV+HLD formats.

terms.definition: The format-specific fantasy decision score shown on a 0-100 scale. Higher is better within the displayed board. MLB and prospect values are aligned at the top, but mixed-player trades are comparable in ballpark rather than to the decimal.

example.text: On the July 26 committed board, Franklin Arias carried a 57.2 ValuCast Value.

terms.definition: A player's position after sorting the current ValuCast board. It is an ordering, not a probability or scouting grade.
The aggregate median rank across the available public boards, shown with the number of boards contributing. It is comparison context only and does not generate ValuCast rank or value.
A tracked call where ValuCast ranks a player materially ahead of the aggregate public consensus. The Ledger records what happened next.
A quality-direction rank inside the stated qualified pool. A 90th-percentile result means the metric graded better than about 90% of that pool; lower-is-better statistics are reversed before ranking.
How stable the displayed read is given sample size, coverage, and uncertainty. It is not the probability that the player succeeds.
What the trusted expected or projected rate evidence supports, kept separate from playing time and role.
Expected plate appearances or innings plus role and availability. Opportunity can change fantasy value without changing the underlying skill read.
A league-settings view that reorders the visible pool using the selected categories. It does not change the public ValuCast Value.
Estimated MLB arrival. A year is player-specific when available; otherwise the display uses a shared level-based window, not a player-specific forecast.
The teams, roster depth, scoring preset, prospect slots, and competitive window supplied for a league-aware decision. Only adjustments the tool explicitly says are calibrated change the totals.
The difference between the value received and value given. A positive margin favors the return side; a margin inside the value band is called even.
The uncertainty tolerance used by The Second Opinion. Margins inside roughly nine points per player are treated as a coin flip, not a win.
terms.formula: about ±9 × players on the larger side

terms.definition: A replacement-adjusted dollar allocation for the supplied teams, budget, and roster depth. Now $ isolates current-season projected production.
The statistics a league counts. ValuCast applies the selected hitting and pitching categories when that format has a validated translation.
A number inferred from available evidence rather than measured directly. ValuCast labels estimates with “est.” and explains their source.
A dash or empty field means the source does not support a trustworthy number. ValuCast leaves it missing rather than inventing an estimate.
The elapsed days between a dated ValuCast call and the later comparison event recorded by Call-Up Receipts.
The change in a player's ValuCast score over the selected archived window. Small moves below the published threshold are omitted.
A held-out live check that compares a challenger projection with the incumbent after a fixed freeze date. It blocks promotion when the evidence does not clear the registered standard.
The Ledger's recorded outcomes: the field moved toward ValuCast, moved away, ValuCast backed off, no decisive move occurred, or the player left the tracked universe through promotion or graduation.
Hits divided by official at-bats.
How often a hitter reaches base through a hit, walk, or hit-by-pitch, with sacrifice flies included in the denominator.
Total bases divided by at-bats; extra-base hits count more than singles.
On-base percentage plus slugging percentage.
Isolated power: extra bases per at-bat after removing singles from slugging.
Strikeouts divided by plate appearances for hitters.
Walks divided by plate appearances.
Earned runs allowed per nine innings.
Walks plus hits allowed per inning pitched.
Strikeouts per nine innings pitched.
Walks allowed per nine innings pitched.
Strikeout percentage minus walk percentage; a compact pitcher dominance and command measure.
The share of pitches at which the hitter swings.
The share of swings that miss.

example.text: One committed High-A sample recorded a 12.7% Whiff% across 728 tracked pitches.

terms.definition: The share of all pitches that produce a swinging strike.
The share of pitches outside the strike zone at which the hitter swings. Samples using pixel calibration are labeled est.
The share of pitches inside the strike zone at which the hitter swings. Samples using pixel calibration are labeled est.
The share of swings at pitches inside the strike zone that make contact. Samples using pixel calibration are labeled est.
The share of pitches classified inside the strike zone. Samples using pixel calibration are labeled est.

example.text: The committed plate-discipline artifact records whether each level sample used calibrated zone locations.
